lead: >-
  Active experiences differ greatly on a journey through Bolivia, Brazil and Peru: walks near Iguazu Falls, an off-road high-altitude route to Uyuni, and excursions among Andean landscapes and Inca heritage sites. Our itineraries also include Argentina and Chile, so the three selected countries do not form a separate continuous route.
---

## Adventures across three countries: what is actually included

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} combining Bolivia, Brazil and Peru with an adventure element. The confirmed itineraries cover **five countries**: Brazil, Argentina, Chile, Bolivia and Peru. The first days are spent by the Atlantic Ocean and Iguazu Falls, before the route continues through Argentina and Chile to the Bolivian lagoons, Uyuni Salt Flat, Lake Titicaca and Machu Picchu.

The main adventure stage is the journey **in 4×4 vehicles across Bolivia's highlands**. Brazil has more developed trails and sightseeing excursions; Peru offers mountain roads, archaeology and visits to Inca monuments. The “Adventure” label alone does not mean that the Inca Trail trek, technical ascents or rafting are included.

If you would like other combinations of countries, explore [multi-country adventure itineraries](/multi-country/interests/adventure/). The [general Bolivia, Brazil and Peru catalogue](/multi-country/bolivia_brazil_peru/) shows programmes without a thematic filter.

## Brazil: tropical forests, Rio and Iguazu

In [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), the programme includes visits to Corcovado and Sugarloaf Mountain by train and cable car. These offer views of the mountainous landscape from above, but they are not sporting ascents. Rio is hot and humid, making even ordinary sightseeing walks feel quite different from days on the Bolivian plateau.

Near [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), the route follows paths and viewpoints beside the cascades, surrounded by humid forest. Some itineraries separately offer the Bird Park and a Macuco Safari boat ride. **An optional excursion is not the same as an included service**: check its availability, price and operating conditions for the specific tour.

Tropical humidity, waterfall spray and convenient walking paths contrast sharply with the later journey through Bolivia's dry highlands. Those seeking more independent active experiences in Brazil can compare [Brazil adventure tours](/interests/adventure/tours/brazil/).

## Bolivia: the true off-road stage

After [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/), the route crosses the Chile–Bolivia border and continues by off-road vehicle. Confirmed stops include [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/) near Licancabur Volcano, the Salvador Dalí Desert, the [Sol de Mañana geysers](/bolivia/place/sol-de-manana-geysers/) and [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/). The road passes through exposed high-altitude landscapes with intense sunshine and cold winds.

Other lagoons follow, along with the salt flats near [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) and [Incahuasi Island](/bolivia/place/incahuasi-island/). In dry weather, the salt flat looks like an endless white plain. After rainfall, some sections are covered in water, and the choice of drivable routes depends on surface conditions. Mirror-like reflections cannot be guaranteed on every day of the year.

This section requires readiness for long drives and high elevations, not climbing skills. The programme specifies off-road vehicles and stops at lagoons, but does not include volcano ascents. If this is your main reason for travelling, consider [adventure itineraries in Bolivia](/interests/adventure/tours/bolivia/), which may allocate a larger share of the trip to highland days.

## Peru: Titicaca and Machu Picchu without a promise of trekking

From La Paz, the journey continues to [Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/), where a visit to the [Uros Islands](/peru/place/uros-islands/) is scheduled. A tourist bus then crosses [La Raya Pass](/peru/place/la-raya-pass/) towards [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/). Mountain scenery accompanies the road and sightseeing stops, but this is not a multi-day walking expedition.

In Cusco, visitors explore [Coricancha](/peru/place/coricancha/) and nearby archaeological complexes before taking an excursion to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). Machu Picchu has several official visitor circuits. Tickets and sightseeing routes should be selected in advance: a standard admission ticket does not grant access to every mountain trail.

This Peruvian finale suits travellers who love highland scenery and Inca history. Anyone wanting a full trekking expedition should look for an itinerary that explicitly includes one rather than treating a sightseeing tour as its equivalent. Compare [adventure tours in Peru](/interests/adventure/tours/peru/).

## How the available options differ

The [18-day group tour across five countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/) combines Rio, Iguazu, the Atacama, Bolivia's off-road section, Titicaca, Cusco and Machu Picchu. Travellers choose it to explore these regions in sequence, accepting the frequent transfers involved.

A [19-day private Carnival itinerary in Rio](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-carnival-private-tour/) adds a festival-focused experience to the first Brazilian days. The [18-day group programme with the Champions' Parade](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-rio-champions-parade-18-days/) also depends on Carnival dates. The [19-day New Year group itinerary](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-new-year-group-tour-19-days/) starts with New Year celebrations in Rio.

When choosing, compare departure dates, group format, guiding languages, rest days and excursions actually included, not just duration. Festival tours should not be assumed to be more physically demanding simply because their calendars are busy.

## Altitude, connections and packing

Different clothing is needed for humid Rio, Iguazu Falls, the Atacama Desert and the Altiplano: lightweight clothes, a waterproof layer, warm clothing for windy conditions and sun protection. Off-road days require time for stops and acclimatisation. Travellers with medical restrictions should discuss high-altitude travel with a doctor.

**The three countries in this selection are part of a longer journey.** In the confirmed itineraries, Argentina and Chile lie between Brazil and Bolivia; the passage from Chile's San Pedro to the Bolivian lagoons includes a land-border crossing. Documents, visa and transit rules must be checked for the complete set of countries, the travellers' passports and actual dates. Currencies and payment methods also vary, so verify whether a particular bank card will work.

We help coordinate flight sequences, overland sections, a suitable pace and the required documents. Shortening the journey to exactly three countries would mean designing a new itinerary, taking account of distances and the loss of some existing excursion days.

## Frequently asked questions about adventures in Bolivia, Brazil and Peru

### Is there a ready-made trip visiting only these three countries?

The main confirmed programmes in this selection visit five countries, including Argentina and Chile. A trip limited to Bolivia, Brazil and Peru would require a revised itinerary and new transport connections.

### Do I need experience of multi-day mountain hikes?

No. In the described options, the Bolivian stage takes place in off-road vehicles and Machu Picchu is visited on a sightseeing excursion. The main considerations are tolerance of high altitude, long journeys and changing weather. Technical trekking is not specified.

### Can I add a boat ride at Iguazu?

Macuco Safari is offered as an extra on certain tours. Check the conditions and whether it is included in your chosen programme. [Excursions around Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/foz-do-iguacu/) provide a separate overview of activity options.

### What has the greatest effect on when to travel?

For Uyuni, weather and access to the salt flat matter; for Machu Picchu, the available official tickets and sightseeing circuit; and for Iguazu, conditions for walking near the falls. Dates for a long itinerary must work across all its sections, not just for one photogenic moment.

lead: >-
  Bolivia, Brazil and Peru in one journey reveal different periods of South American history: Rio de Janeiro's cultural landscape, pre-Inca Tiwanaku and the Inca heritage of Cusco and Machu Picchu. ## Three different histories within one longer itinerary

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} combining Bolivia, Brazil and Peru with a cultural and historical programme. The confirmed itineraries featuring this trio continue **through Argentina and Chile**. It therefore makes more sense to compare the cultural experiences offered by the three selected countries than to imagine a standalone flight straight from Rio to La Paz.

In Brazil, travellers discover Rio and its Portuguese colonial heritage. Bolivia introduces the pre-Inca centre of Tiwanaku and everyday life in high-altitude La Paz. Peru concludes the historical sequence with Cusco, Inca sanctuaries and Machu Picchu. The general [catalogue of trips to Bolivia, Brazil and Peru](/multi-country/bolivia_brazil_peru/) also covers other interests; here the focus is archaeology, urban culture and the significance of each historical stop.

## Rio de Janeiro: a city between the ocean and mountains

The cultural day in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) includes trips up Corcovado and Sugarloaf Mountain and an introduction to historic neighbourhoods. In the old centre, attention turns to colonial buildings, churches and cathedrals; from the viewpoints, the city unfolds against the mountains and Guanabara Bay.

UNESCO recognises this setting as a cultural landscape shaped by the relationship between the city, forested mountains and the sea. Rio is therefore worth exploring beyond its façades: its former capital's port setting, neighbourhoods and public spaces make more sense after visiting the scenic viewpoints.

On the [18-day five-country tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/), Rio occupies the first few days. The [private Carnival itinerary](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-carnival-private-tour/) adds the Sambadrome and a Carnival performance to the city excursions. The [Champions' Parade tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-rio-champions-parade-18-days/) likewise puts the cultural emphasis on the event. **Carnival attendance is not automatically included in every tour** that visits Rio.

Next comes [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). The waterfalls are primarily a nature stop. They are important to the complete journey, but should not be counted as an additional lesson in Brazilian history. Other ways to discover the country's culture are featured in [Brazil's cultural and historical tours](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/brazil/).

## Bolivia: La Paz and Tiwanaku before the Incas

After Chile's Atacama, the itineraries cross highland Bolivia. The journey begins with lagoons and the Uyuni Salt Flat before continuing to [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/). A sightseeing tour introduces historic districts, city markets and the city's dramatic location among steep mountain slopes. This stage offers a glimpse of contemporary Andean urban culture, unlike the archaeological stops that follow.

On the way to Peru, the route visits [Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/). Here are the Gateway of the Sun, structures belonging to a ceremonial complex and remains of a city that served as the political and religious centre of an independent pre-Inca civilisation. Its flourishing long preceded the expansion of the Inca state. Visiting **before Cusco** is particularly valuable because it makes clear that the pre-Columbian history of the Andes did not begin with the Incas.

Tiwanaku has its own architectural forms and concepts of sacred space; it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It should not be described as “Inca ruins” simply because the next section of the trip is in Peru. With [cultural and historical tours in Bolivia](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/bolivia/), you can explore this subject in greater depth and spend less time on long transfers.

## Peru: Titicaca, Cusco's sacred history and Machu Picchu

After crossing the border, the itinerary passes through [Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/). Programmes include a visit to the [floating Uros Islands](/peru/place/uros-islands/). This introduces the living tradition of inhabiting reed islands, not an archaeological monument from the Tiwanaku period. The present-day lives of local people deserve to be considered separately from the history of ancient states.

The road to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) is a sightseeing transfer stopping at Andahuaylillas, Raqchi, La Raya Pass and other places. Andahuaylillas is associated with colonial church art, while Raqchi is known for Inca architecture. One day's journey reveals the transition from pre-Hispanic buildings to the colonial period.

In Cusco, the route explores [Coricancha](/peru/place/coricancha/) and archaeological sites around the city. The main separate excursion is to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/), where the design of Inca terraces and structures is experienced alongside the mountain terrain. Visitors must choose an official circuit and entry time in advance. Different circuits offer different experiences; having a ticket does not grant access to every part of the site.

For a deeper exploration of Andean history, compare [cultural and historical tours in Peru](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/peru/) rather than choosing a five-country programme purely for its country count.

## Why the “Tiwanaku to Cusco” sequence is especially valuable

Travellers often associate the entire history of the Andes with the Incas. This combination reveals a longer chronology: an ancient centre in Bolivia, living traditions around Titicaca, Inca architecture in Cusco and Machu Picchu, followed by Lima's Spanish colonial heritage. **Every stop answers a different question**, which is why the archaeological day at Tiwanaku deserves as much attention as the famous Peruvian site.

The practical trade-off is equally clear. Between Rio and Bolivia, the ready-made journey includes separate days in Argentina and Chile, while Bolivia itself has numerous nature stops reached by off-road vehicle. Travellers who want more museums and fewer hours driving across the Altiplano should discuss a different balance.

The [19-day five-country New Year programme](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-new-year-group-tour-19-days/) adds a festive beginning in Brazil. It retains Tiwanaku, Titicaca and Peru's archaeological section, but its dates are tied to the New Year period. Compare the included excursions, guiding languages and actual time allocated to each historical visit for the particular tour.

## What to agree before booking

A rewarding cultural trip requires enough time at each site and for transfers between them, not merely a long list of names. Machu Picchu uses a ticketing system with multiple visitor circuits; museum visits and access to individual archaeological areas depend on the selected programme and available entry sessions.

The ready-made route from Brazil to Bolivia passes through Argentina and Chile. Document checks must therefore cover the entire journey, including flights and land borders. We help coordinate the sequence of cities, excursions, transfers, tickets and a comfortable pace based on the historical sites that matter most to each traveller.

## Frequently asked questions about the history of Bolivia, Brazil and Peru

### Is there a ready-made journey visiting exactly three countries?

The suitable existing programmes include five countries, with Argentina and Chile in addition. A trip limited to Bolivia, Brazil and Peru would require arranging separate flights and allocating days between Rio, Tiwanaku, Cusco and Machu Picchu.

### How is Tiwanaku different from Machu Picchu?

[Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/) was the centre of an independent pre-Inca civilisation on the Altiplano. [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) is associated with the Inca state and lies in a different natural and historical setting. Visiting both reveals distinct periods of Andean history.

### Is Carnival included in culture-focused tours through Rio?

Only in programmes that explicitly list the Carnival event, such as the [private five-country Carnival tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-carnival-private-tour/). An ordinary visit to Rio and its historic centre does not include a parade ticket.

### Can I see Machu Picchu and the Uros Islands on one trip?

Yes. Both stops feature in the confirmed five-country routes: first [Titicaca and Uros](/peru/place/uros-islands/), then Cusco and Machu Picchu. Check the sequence and included services in your chosen tour.

## Brazil, Bolivia and Peru: from celebrations in Rio to ancient Andean cities

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} featuring Brazil, Bolivia and Peru under the “Events and Festivals” theme. **Every suitable itinerary begins with a scheduled event in Rio**, after which the journey gradually moves towards the highlands and Andean heritage sites. In these particular trips, Bolivia and Peru are not presented as destinations for attending local festivals.

The selection title highlights three main countries, but the actual programmes also visit Argentina and Chile. The journey first heads to Iguazu and Buenos Aires, then continues via Santiago and the Atacama to the Bolivian Altiplano. Only afterwards come [Lake Titicaca in Peru](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/), [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and Lima.

This selection is therefore useful for choosing **a festival trip that ends with an extensive journey through Peru**, not for finding a separate direct Rio–La Paz–Machu Picchu tour. See the broader geography in the [Brazil, Bolivia and Peru catalogue](/multi-country/bolivia_brazil_peru/).

## Three different ways to begin with an event

| Programme | Main event |
|---|---|
| [New Year in Rio and five countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-new-year-group-tour-19-days/) | Copacabana, December 31 |
| [Carnival in Rio and five countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-carnival-private-tour/) | Carnival evening at the Sambadrome |
| [Champions' Parade and five countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-rio-champions-parade-18-days/) | Performances by Carnival winners |

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_5_stran_latinskoj_ameriki_na_16_dnej_na_novyj_god,tour_source_karnaval_5_stran,tour_source_5_stran_latinskoj_ameriki_i_parad_chempionov_karnavala}}

The New Year programme lasts 19 days, starting on December 30 and celebrating New Year's Eve on Copacabana. The private Carnival itinerary also lasts 19 days, but is tied to Carnival. Another group option, lasting 18 days, includes the Champions' Parade.

For **Carnival 2027**, LIESA announced the main parades for February 7–9 and the Champions' Parade for February 13. The specific event must be confirmed separately from other services: an official calendar does not automatically confirm a place on a tour or a particular ticket category.

## Brazil: a festive night and the start of a long journey

In [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), travellers take excursions to Corcovado and Sugarloaf Mountain. Depending on the option, the programme includes either New Year on the beach or a visit to the Sambadrome. These experiences cannot be swapped freely within an existing itinerary because they fall on different dates.

Next come the [waterfalls at Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). The programme covers both the Brazilian and Argentine sides of the falls, followed by Buenos Aires. Argentina does not appear in this selection's title, but remains an important stage of the actual trip. After Buenos Aires, the journey continues towards Santiago and then the Atacama.

This matters when planning time to rest: after the celebrations, the trip does not become a relaxed short holiday. Many flights, excursions and changes of climate still lie ahead.

## Bolivia: reaching Uyuni and Titicaca

The high-altitude section starts after [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) in Chile, from where the route approaches the Bolivian border. A jeep tour through lagoons and the Altiplano visits [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). The journey then continues to La Paz and via Tiwanaku towards Lake Titicaca.

For most travellers, the principal challenge here is **the altitude and long drives**. After tropical Rio, Iguazu and South American cities, the temperature, humidity and road conditions change sharply. Check your personal tolerance of altitude and discuss a suitable pace with the tour organiser in advance.

The condition of the salt flat and roads depends on rainfall. During the rainy season, individual sections may need to be travelled differently; specific water reflections and road conditions cannot be guaranteed in advance. A fixed Carnival or New Year date therefore needs to be paired with reasonable flexibility for the nature stops.

## Peru: Puno, Cusco and Machu Picchu after Bolivia's lagoons

After Bolivia, the trip continues through [Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/) towards [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). The emphasis shifts to Inca history, high-altitude cities and archaeology. The itinerary concludes in Lima.

The Peruvian stage is more than a spare day added to the journey. It includes transfers, excursions, a rail journey towards Machu Picchu and a return to the airport. Those activities need adequate time whenever the festival-related beginning of the trip is adjusted.

Access to Machu Picchu depends on the agreed entry time, visitor circuit and official tickets. Moving the visit to another day may affect the train and accommodation. It would therefore be misleading to promise unlimited flexibility in rearranging the programme after booking.

## Different seasons in one journey

The date of the main event shapes conditions throughout the sequence. New Year on Copacabana falls during the Southern Hemisphere summer. Carnival takes place at another time, shifting the arrival dates in Uyuni and the Peruvian Andes as well. Heat and humidity matter in Rio, altitude and cold nights on the Altiplano, and wetter or drier periods in Cusco and Machu Picchu. A single seasonal recommendation for the entire five-country trip would be inaccurate.

Practical packing includes lightweight clothing for Rio, warm layers and wind protection for the highlands, and waterproof items and suitable footwear for nature excursions. The more important issue is not luggage weight in isolation, but restrictions on the different flights and convenience during overland transfers.

Documents also need to be checked for **all five countries**, not only the three in the title. The itinerary includes multiple border crossings and a combination of air and land transport. Entry rules, insurance, payment options and operating conditions at particular parks depend on nationality and travel date.

## Choosing between a festival-focused trip and a Peru-focused trip

If New Year or Carnival is your main priority, choose the event date and format first, then decide whether the subsequent Andean journey suits you. If Machu Picchu and Inca culture matter more, compare [tours of Peru](/peru/tour/) and [cultural journeys](/interests/culture-and-history/), which depend less on Rio's festival dates.

We can help coordinate the itinerary, flight logistics, ground transfers and excursion schedule. However, this thematic selection does not imply a guaranteed visa, admission to a particular parade or unchanging mountain weather.

## Frequently asked questions about festival trips through Brazil, Bolivia and Peru

### Which country hosts the event around which the itinerary is organised?

Brazil, specifically Rio de Janeiro. In Bolivia and Peru, the confirmed activities are nature and heritage stops rather than festival attendance.

### Can I fly to Peru immediately after Carnival?

The ready-made journeys travel via Iguazu, Argentina, Chile and Bolivia. A shorter sequence would require a private itinerary and a different quotation.

### Why does the itinerary spend several days in Bolivia?

To complete the jeep route through high-altitude lagoons, see the Uyuni Salt Flat and then continue towards Titicaca. This is a substantial part of the journey, not a brief transit stop.

### What determines a visit to Machu Picchu?

Agreed dates, visitor route and entry time, transport arrangements and official tickets. In an extensive five-country tour, this stage must be planned together with flights and the highland section.

## How a food-focused journey through three countries works

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. The main itinerary is the [20-day journey through six Latin American countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/). It starts in Brazil, continues through Argentina, Uruguay and Chile, then takes travellers through Bolivia to Peru. Selecting Bolivia, Brazil and Peru in the filter means **all three are on the main route**, not that the tour is limited to them.

Food experiences here complement sightseeing and exploring the cities. The timetable in the three selected countries does not include a separate cookery workshop, winery visit or fixed series of tastings. It does, however, provide convenient city stops where travellers can explore regional dishes independently or arrange an additional gastronomic experience in advance. Browse [multi-country food and wine journeys](/multi-country/interests/food-and-wine/) to compare other geographic combinations.

## Brazil: dining in Rio before visiting the waterfalls

In [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), the itinerary concentrates on Corcovado, Sugarloaf Mountain and city attractions. It is the most convenient Brazilian stage for discovering local food: a restaurant dinner or market visit is easier to discuss on a day staying in the city than on a flight day. Brazilian cuisine here draws on beans, rice, cassava, tropical fruit and fish dishes; choosing a particular restaurant and meal remains up to the traveller.

The next stop is Iguazu, devoted to the waterfalls and crossing to the Argentine side. It would be misleading to turn this busy nature day into a promised gastronomic excursion. If food and local dining are a priority, make time in Rio rather than adding a mandatory stop near the waterfalls.

## Bolivia: food and wellbeing at altitude

After Chile comes the jeep route through high-altitude lagoons, [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/) and [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). Here, meals are shaped primarily by the road, expedition-style accommodation and the availability of stops. The journey reaches elevations above 4,000 metres. Water, familiar snacks and an agreed meal schedule are more useful on this section than planning a lengthy tasting immediately after crossing the border.

In [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/), the itinerary allows some time in the city, including a sightseeing excursion and a visit to the Witches' Market. It is a cultural site, and there is no basis for describing it as a gastronomic market with an included tasting. To explore Bolivian cuisine separately, you could discuss a restaurant dinner or city walk focused on Andean foods. Any such addition needs to fit the available time and conditions of the particular day.

The journey to Peru passes through [Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/) and the Titicaca region. The excursion and border-crossing schedule takes priority over lingering over lunch. Altitude sickness can occur as elevation increases, so the pace of ascent and individual wellbeing must be considered.

## Peru: how Cusco differs from Lima

The Peruvian section begins near Lake Titicaca, followed by the [Uros Islands](/peru/place/uros-islands/), the journey to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) and a visit to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). Potatoes, maize and other local crops underpin many traditional Andean dishes. But visits to heritage sites and long journeys by tourist bus leave little room for spontaneous food-focused detours.

The final stop, [Lima](/peru/place/lima/), where the programme includes city sightseeing, is better suited to a more relaxed exploration of Peruvian food. With sufficient time, a dinner featuring Peruvian dishes can be arranged separately, taking dietary restrictions and preferences into account. A breakfast or lunch mentioned in the programme should not automatically be presented as a full tasting experience.

| Country | Best day to choose |
|---|---|
| Brazil | Time in the city of Rio |
| Bolivia | La Paz, after the highland stage |
| Peru | Lima, after the Andean sightseeing |

## Where the longer programme actually features wine

During the stop in Santiago, Chile, the six-country tour offers **an optional winery excursion to the [Maipo Valley](/chile/place/maipo-valley/) with a tasting**. It costs extra and must be arranged in advance. This takes place in Chile, a fourth country outside the selected combination of Bolivia, Brazil and Peru.

The programme also features a tango show with dinner in Argentina. That can count as a gastronomic episode of the larger journey, but it cannot be transferred to the list of included activities in Brazil, Bolivia or Peru. Travellers who are primarily interested in wine should compare [food and wine tours featuring Chile](/interests/food-and-wine/tours/chile/) and consider how much time is actually allocated to wineries.

## Adding worthwhile food stops to the itinerary

Ada Tours can discuss private changes to the programme: where to allow a free evening, whether there is time for a local restaurant, which separate tastings you want, and which day can accommodate them without losing an included excursion. These arrangements need to be made before booking. Days involving an international flight, high-altitude transfer or Machu Picchu visit are poorly suited to an additional lengthy activity.

Travellers with allergies, special diets or food restrictions should agree meal arrangements for each stage, particularly the remote stops in Bolivia. Animal and plant products should not be carried freely between countries without checking current customs and sanitary regulations. The [Bolivia, Brazil and Peru overview](/multi-country/bolivia_brazil_peru/) helps put the rest of the journey's logistics in context.

## Frequently asked questions about food in Bolivia, Brazil and Peru

### Are food tastings included in each of the three countries?

No. Gastronomy is listed as a secondary interest within a larger tour, but special tastings in Brazil, Bolivia and Peru are not among the confirmed included excursions. Separate visits must be arranged.

### Does the journey include a real winery?

Yes, there is an option to visit wineries in Chile's Maipo Valley. This excursion is outside the selected three countries, is not automatically included and is paid for separately.

### Where is it best to make free time for local food?

A full restaurant evening is easier to arrange in Rio or Lima, while La Paz is an option for discovering highland city cuisine after the journey. Specific time slots need to be checked against flights and excursion times.

### Can the tour be limited to Bolivia, Brazil and Peru?

The current suitable tour visits six countries. A programme limited strictly to three countries requires changes to the itinerary and a separate calculation of logistics and services. The original tour already has an established route and duration.

## Bolivia, Brazil and Peru: three countries' natural landscapes on a longer journey

**Iguazu Falls, the Uyuni Salt Flat and Lake Titicaca reveal three very different South American landscapes.** Brazil's humid subtropical forest gives way to Bolivia's exposed high-altitude plains before the journey continues along the Andes through Peru. [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) completes the sequence with a mountain setting where historic terraces are surrounded by green slopes.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with a nature focus, in which all three countries form part of the main route. **These are not journeys restricted to exactly three countries.** For example, the five-country programmes first visit Brazil, Argentina and Chile, then cross Bolivia and finish in Peru. Longer journeys may also add Uruguay, Ecuador and Colombia. The catalogue title names the combination of interest; the exact sequence is explained on each tour page.

If you would rather devote the trip to one type of scenery, first compare [nature tours in Brazil](/interests/nature/tours/brazil/), [Bolivia](/interests/nature/tours/bolivia/) and [Peru](/interests/nature/tours/peru/). A longer cross-border itinerary offers more contrasts, but fewer days at each individual natural attraction.

## Brazil: Rio's green mountains and the cascades of Iguazu

In [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), natural scenery is visible even on city sightseeing excursions. The road to Corcovado passes through the forest of [Tijuca National Park](/brazil/place/tijuca-national-park/); Sugarloaf Mountain offers views across the bay, mountain slopes and ocean. This introduces the city's natural geography rather than providing a separate hike through the forest.

The main standalone nature stop in the Brazilian section is [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). Viewing paths provide panoramic views of the cascades and surrounding forest. The programmes also visit the Argentine side from [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/): the paths are arranged differently, giving visitors two perspectives on the same waterfall complex. Both national parks preserve areas of subtropical forest.

Iguazu's forests are rich in biodiversity, but **the presence of wild animals in the park does not guarantee a sighting**. The principal confirmed experiences on these tours are the waterfalls and forest views. For dedicated animal watching, explore the separate [Wildlife and Safari theme](/interests/wildlife/).

## Bolivia: Altiplano lagoons and the Uyuni Salt Flat

After [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) in Chile, the suitable itineraries begin the Bolivian high-altitude jeep section. It visits [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/), the Sol de Mañana geyser area and [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/). Some days mention flamingos, mineral lakes and volcanic views. The route then continues through other lagoons, stretches of salt flats and [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/).

This nature journey takes place mainly in off-road vehicles with stops along the way. It should not automatically be described as a multi-day trekking expedition. At the same time, travelling by vehicle does not remove the effects of altitude, sunshine, wind and dry air. Even a short walk on the Altiplano feels different from walking beside Iguazu.

Uyuni's surface changes with weather and the amount of water present. Its famous mirror effect depends on particular conditions; **it cannot be promised for every month and date**. It makes more sense to choose a trip based on route accessibility and the confirmed time allocated to nature stops than on a photograph of the reflected sky.

## Peru: Titicaca, Cusco and Machu Picchu's natural setting

From Bolivia, the current itineraries continue towards [Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/). The lake's open water and high-altitude shores provide a striking contrast to Bolivia's dry lakes. However, a visit to the Uros Islands is primarily about local culture and ways of life, and should not be presented as a separate wildlife expedition.

Next come Cusco and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/), surrounded by steep mountain slopes and cloud forests on the eastern side of the Andes. This is both a natural and a cultural heritage site: the landscape is as important as the historic architecture, but the actual tour day usually focuses on an organised visit to the archaeological complex. A sporting trek along the Inca Trail or a separate summit hike should not be assumed included unless specifically stated.

**Nature here is inseparable from history and culture.** If mountains and lakes are your motivation for travelling, check how much time is allocated to being outdoors compared with city excursions and transport.

## Altitude, clothing and border crossings

After Brazil, travellers ascend into regions where elevation has a noticeable effect on wellbeing. La Paz, Cusco and the Bolivian lagoons require attention to acclimatisation. Those with heart or lung problems, or a previous negative experience at altitude, should discuss the route with a doctor. Avoid planning strenuous activity immediately after a rapid ascent.

For the Brazilian section, bring protection against sun and humidity and comfortable shoes with non-slip soles. For the Altiplano, pack warm layers and protection against wind and intense sunshine. The same luggage must work both in warm, humid weather and on cold mornings at altitude. Check baggage restrictions for the particular booked flights.

These itineraries cross several borders, so check the rules for each traveller's nationality, any repeated entries and the actual country sequence. Conditions can differ even between neighbouring states. Ada Tours helps coordinate transfers and the order of visits; legal requirements should be checked against current official regulations before travelling.

## Frequently asked questions about nature in Bolivia, Brazil and Peru

### Can I visit only the three named countries in this selection?

No. The existing itineraries matching the filter also pass through Argentina and Chile, with some covering additional countries. The filter indicates that the desired destinations are included, not that the journey is limited to them.

### Will I have to complete a difficult mountain hike?

The theme name alone does not imply a mandatory multi-day trek. On these itineraries, highland Bolivia is explored by jeep and Machu Picchu is visited on a sightseeing excursion. Nevertheless, altitude, long roads and walks along prepared routes still require physical effort.

### Are flamingo and other wildlife sightings guaranteed?

No. The Bolivian lagoons provide natural habitats for watching birds, and the Iguazu parks are rich in wildlife, but actual sightings depend on season and animal behaviour. Choose dedicated [wildlife-watching tours](/interests/wildlife/tours/) based on their stated programme.
